name: desktop-pet
description: A little companion on the Windows desktop, always on top and in front of borderless games: a cardboard box or one of twelve figures (cat, dog, fox, bunny, hamster, owl, penguin, frog, axolotl, dragon, robot, ghost; cat, dog and bunny in nine coats). It says in a speech bubble what Claude is doing and sums up each answer; Claude's questions, Next Steps' suggestions and reply options are buttons in the bubble, and with typing on a hotkey opens a box to answer without leaving the game. A click on the pet shows the last answer in short; an unanswered bubble shrinks to one line. Optionally one pet per active session, each with its own figure and a name tag, asleep while its prompt cache is cold; it warns before the cache goes cold. Built once with the C# compiler that ships with Windows and signed when a signing script is there. /pet shows it, /pet cat calico picks a figure, /pet stop sends it off.
